name: ProEventsWP
author: accomplicehq

sections.description:
ProEventsWP is a free WordPress event calendar plugin built for the block editor. Create events, organize venues and organizers, and display your calendar in six views. Use WordPress blocks to design event feeds and choose which event details to show.

Free features include:

  • Display events in Month, Week, Day, List, Photo or Map view.
  • Create one-time, all-day and multi-day events, with event timezones and daily opening hours.
  • Repeat events daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. Set exceptions and edit individual occurrences or a series.
  • Design event feeds with WordPress Query Loop patterns, editable event cards and pagination.
  • Help visitors find events with keyword, date, category, tag, venue and organizer filters.
  • Add venues, organizers, categories, tags, event status, costs and website links.
  • Collect individual RSVPs, set capacity limits, send confirmations and let attendees cancel. Keep attendee details private.
  • Show event locations on maps, enter addresses manually or enable optional address lookup.
  • Import CSV and ICS files as event drafts for review.
  • Let visitors download events or add them to their calendars. Include structured event data and access events through a public read-only REST API.

All Free features work without a paid license. Your events and settings stay in your WordPress database when you deactivate or uninstall the plugin.

Visit the ProEventsWP website or try the live demos.

External services and privacy

Freemius

The bundled Freemius SDK provides optional licensing, account, checkout, and update services. Its opt-in screen explains the data shared before optional usage tracking is enabled. Basic Free functionality works without opting in or purchasing a license. Freemius handles paid downloads, subscriptions, and license management.

Privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/

Maps and map tiles

Map scripts are bundled locally. When a visitor opens a map, their browser requests tiles or styles from the configured provider, disclosing normal request information such as their IP address. The default map uses OpenStreetMap tiles. Administrators can configure another provider; its terms and privacy policy apply. Maps display attribution. Address text and external map links remain available when JavaScript or WebGL2 is unavailable.

OpenStreetMap privacy policy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy
OpenStreetMap tile usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/

Optional Geoapify address lookup

Address lookup is disabled by default and needs an administrator-configured Geoapify key. After three typed characters, it sends the editor’s address query to api.geoapify.com to suggest locations. Manual entry works without it. No geocoding request is made merely by saving an event or viewing its page.

Privacy policy: https://www.geoapify.com/privacy-policy/
Terms: https://www.geoapify.com/terms-and-conditions/
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for ProEventsWP, then install and activate it.
  2. Go to Events and create your first event. Add dates, times and other details, plus a venue or organizer if needed.
  3. Edit a page and insert a Month, Week, Day, List, Photo or Map block. You can also use an Event Query pattern to build an event feed.
  4. Use event detail blocks, such as Event Date & Time, Event Venue and Event Schedule, to control how event information appears.

With a block theme, use Appearance > Editor to customize the supplied event, venue, organizer and series templates. Templates you have already customized remain in place. Shortcodes such as [pcwp_calendar] are also available.
sections.faq:
Can I use my existing theme?

Yes. Use the blocks and shortcodes with your theme. A block theme also lets you design event templates in the Site Editor.

Can I create recurring events?

Yes. Free includes daily, weekly, monthly and yearly recurrence, with exceptions. You can edit an individual occurrence or a series.

Can one multi-day event have different hours each day?

Yes. Choose Daily schedule in Event details, enter hours for each date, and mark closed dates. Use the Event Schedule block to display the hours. Daily schedules are available for standalone events.

What does RSVP registration include?

Visitors can register for an event, receive a confirmation and cancel their registration. You can set a capacity limit and manage attendees privately. Each registration reserves one place; payment processing and ticket sales are not included.

Do I need an external service for basic event management?

No. Events, schedules, feeds, filters, imports and calendar downloads work locally. Maps and optional address lookup use the external services described below.

Does uninstalling delete my events?

No. Your events, settings and plugin tables are kept to prevent accidental data loss.

How do I get support?

Use the WordPress.org support forum for Free support. Product inquiries and paid support can be sent to par@accomplice.se.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Improved security for event structured data, event creation and public venue and organizer details.
  • Brought plugin settings together under Events > Settings and kept existing settings links working.
  • Improved translation loading and made settings panels easier to use on smaller screens and with assistive technology.

1.1.0

  • Added Free recurring events with daily, weekly, monthly and yearly rules, exceptions and date previews.
  • Added six Free calendar views: Month, Week, Day, List, Photo and Map, with editable event feeds in List and Photo.
  • Added venue and organizer filters, customizable templates, grouped map markers and calendar sharing and subscriptions.
  • Added individual RSVPs with capacity limits, confirmations, cancellation and private attendee management.
  • Made event details, daily schedules and RSVP settings easier to edit.

1.0.0

  • Introduced event management, event feeds, Month and Day calendars, and daily schedules.
  • Added venues, organizers, event maps, CSV and ICS imports, calendar downloads and structured event data.
